Expected change site: tests/test_verify_integration_fingerprints_tiers.py wired into the CI test allowlists in .github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml, and .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml.

However, grep for 'test_verify_integration_fingerprints_tiers' across .github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml, and .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml returns zero matches. The existing CI convention is explicit python3 tests/<file>.py invocations (e.g., ci.yml lines 109-183, test-and-mark-stable.yml lines 1854, 2120-3246). The new test file is never invoked by any workflow, making the tier regression coverage dead code that cannot catch failures in ratio/count_only/warn_only logic.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
File: scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py
Line or code reference: lines 798-807 (the `_issue_tier_violation_message` function added in original_pr_diff, modified in last_run_diff.patch)
Problem: The ratio case hard-codes the string 'ratio' in the message template, while the else branch now uses `tier_name = tier or "count_only"` correctly. When tier="warn_only", the message still incorrectly says "verification tier 'count_only'" for the non-ratio path.
Why it fails at runtime: Downstream tooling, tests, or log parsers that match exact tier names will be misled when warn_only tier violations are reported - the message will incorrectly report "count_only".
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

File: scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh
Line or code reference: _select_fingerprint_verification_tier function (lines 482-530 in original_pr_diff)
Problem: When the Python tier selector fails (non-zero exit or JSON parse error), the shell falls back to strict mode but RESOLVER_FP_VERIFICATION_TIER_REASON is only set on the success path. The later guard `if [ "${RESOLVER_FP_VERIFICATION_TIER:-strict}" = "warn_only" ]` can then behave incorrectly after selection errors.
Why it fails at runtime: A transient failure in tier selection could leave the reason variable stale, potentially causing incorrect behavior in the warn_only persistence guard logic.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

Evidence of absence: tests/test_verify_integration_fingerprints_tiers.py exists with 234 lines covering strict, ratio, count_only, and warn_only tiers, but it is not referenced in any CI workflow. The test file uses direct python3 invocation rather than being part of the allowlisted test suite.

Requirement: "add `--verification-tier <strict|ratio|count_only|warn_only>` to `scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py`; wire resolver-side tier selection in `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh`; emit `FINGERPRINT_TIER_DOWNGRADED_V1` markers whenever the selected tier changes and cover each tier with focused tests."
Expected change site: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/mark-stable.yml`, `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml`
Evidence of absence: The new test file `tests/test_verify_integration_fingerprints_tiers.py` exists with comprehensive coverage for all four tiers (strict, ratio, count_only, warn_only), but is not referenced in any CI workflow file. The file contains 8 test functions covering: default/explicit strict matching, ratio pass/fail at 95% threshold, count_only pass/fail with at-least-one-match semantics, warn_only suppression and marker emission, compare mode with ratio tier, and invalid tier rejection. The issue explicitly requires "cover each tier with focused tests" which implies these tests must be executable in CI. The PR implements the verification logic correctly but fails to wire the tests into the CI allowlists, rendering the test coverage ineffective for regression prevention.

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
File: scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py
Line or code reference: _issue_tier_violation_message (lines ~798-810, specifically the else branch added/hardened in last_run_diff.patch)
Problem: The else branch sets tier_name = tier or "count_only" but the ratio branch still hard-codes the literal string 'ratio' inside the f-string. When tier="warn_only" or "count_only", the emitted diagnostic message can still claim the wrong tier name.
Why it fails at runtime: Downstream log parsers, test assertions, or human triage that match exact tier names (or the downgrade marker) will receive misleading text, breaking observability of which tier actually applied. The last autofix only partially hardened one branch.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

File: scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh
Line or code reference: _select_fingerprint_verification_tier (~lines 482-530 in PR diff) and the Python inline block that duplicates select_verification_tier_from_pr_payload
Problem: The shell wrapper and the Python helper inside it duplicate nearly-identical tier-selection logic (including the same _parse_nonnegative_int and _select_tier patterns). The inline Python block does not call the shared Python function introduced in the same PR.
Why it fails at runtime: Maintenance divergence is guaranteed. A future change to one path (e.g. adjusting the 95% ratio threshold or adding a new tier) will silently leave the other path stale, violating the "keep changes local to verifier/resolver logic" constraint and the intent of a single source of truth for tier semantics.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

File: scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py
Line or code reference: main() argument parser (~lines 1519-1532)
Problem: The --verification-tier missing-argument branch prints "::error::..." to stdout (via print(..., file=sys.stderr) is only on the later unsupported-tier path). The parser falls through to rc=2 but the error annotation is not guaranteed to be picked up by GitHub Actions error surface.
Why it fails at runtime: When a caller supplies an incomplete flag (e.g. a malformed workflow_dispatch), the error is invisible in the Actions UI "Errors" section, delaying diagnosis of misconfiguration. This is a regression introduced by the new CLI option.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

Requirement: "add focused test coverage for each tier" and the explicit Phase 3 scope that the new test file must be wired into CI so the coverage actually runs.
Expected change site: .github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml, .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml (or the test harness that runs explicit python3 tests/<file>.py commands)
Evidence of absence: tests/test_verify_integration_fingerprints_tiers.py exists, contains comprehensive tests for strict/ratio/count_only/warn_only (including downgrade markers and compare mode), but is absent from every CI allowlist and is never executed by the release gate (confirmed by the Copilot and Gemini reviewer comments and the lack of any import/exec in existing test files). The linked issue and plan both require this coverage to be active.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

Requirement: "No agents.md / README.md edits in this issue" was followed, but the duplication of tier-selection logic between the shell wrapper and the verifier violates the "stay inside files_touched and keep the change local to verifier/resolver logic"
